facts.statement: Tsagantegia is a genus of medium-sized ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Tsagantegia (; meaning Tsagan Teg) is a genus of medium-sized ankylosaurid thyreophoran dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Tsagantegia is a very partial individual consisting solely of a skull, with no postcranial remains.
facts.quote: The specimen consists of a very partial individual, comprising the skull and lacking postcranial remains.

facts.statement: Tsagantegia is characterized by an elongated snout and flattened facial osteoderms, which differ greatly from other ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: Since it only preserves the skull, Tsagantegia is mainly characterized by its elongated snout and the flattened facial osteoderms, greatly differing from other ankylosaurs.

facts.statement: The skull remained unresearched until it was formally described by Russian paleontologist Tatiana Tumanova in 1993.
facts.quote: This skull remained unresearched until it was described by Russian paleontologist Tatiana Tumanova in 1993.

facts.statement: Tumanova described the skull as a new genus and species, Tsagantegia longicranialis.
facts.quote: Tumanova described the skull as belonging to a new genus and species of ankylosaurine ankylosaurid, Tsagantegia longicranialis.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the Tsagan-Teg locality, while the species name means "long-skulled" in Latin.
facts.quote: The generic name, Tsagantegia, is in reference to the Tsagan-Teg locality where the skull was unearthed, and the specific name, longicranialis, comes from the Latin roots longus "long" and cranium "skull" in reference to its elongated skull.

facts.statement: Tsagantegia was a medium to large ankylosaur estimated to be 6 to 7 meters long and weigh 1 to 4 tons.
facts.quote: Tsagantegia was a medium to large-sized ankyosaur, with an estimated length of 6 to 7 m and weighing about 1 to 4 t.

facts.statement: Unlike other Asian ankylosaurs, the cranial ornamentation of Tsagantegia is amorphous and flattened rather than a mosaic of polygons.
facts.quote: Unlike other Asian ankylosaurs, in Tsagantegia the caputegulae (cranial ornamentation) are not subdivided into a mosaic of polygons but are amorphous and flattened; they show some degree of symmetry.

facts.statement: The age of the Bayan Shireh Formation, where Tsagantegia was found, is confirmed to be between 92 and 86 million years ago.
facts.quote: Calcite U–Pb analyses seem to confirm the age of the Bayan Shireh Formation from 92 million to 86 million years ago, Cenomanian-Santonian ages.

facts.statement: The environment where Tsagantegia lived was semi-arid with large rivers and lakes.
facts.quote: Caliche-based boundary indicates a semi-arid environment and climate, but also, the presence of fluvial and lacustrine sediments are indicators of large rivers and lakes.

facts.statement: Comparisons with Talarurus suggest Tsagantegia was a browser herbivore, whereas Talarurus was a grazer.
facts.quote: Based on comparisons between the snouts of Tsagantegia and the contemporary Talarurus, these taxa were divided by niche partitioning. In a palatal view, the rostra Talarurus have a broad-like, rectangular shape, while Tsagantegia have a more shovel-like shaped rostra. These morphological differences indicate that Tsagantegia filled the niche of a browser herbivore, while Talarurus was a grazer.

facts.statement: Tsagantegia is classified within the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Ankylosauridae

facts.statement: A 2012 analysis found that Tsagantegia was closely related to Pinacosaurus and Shamosaurus.
facts.quote: En 2012, Thompson et al. realizó un análisis de casi todos los anquilosáuridos válidos conocidos y taxones externos en ese momento. Basaron su filogenia resultante en caracteres que representan la anatomía craneal, poscraneal y osteodérmica y detalles de sinapomorfias para cada clado recuperado. Se descubrió que Tsagantegia estaba estrechamente relacionado con Pinacosaurus y Shamosaurus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Tsagantegia belongs to the subfamily Shamosaurinae or is a basal member of Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: Por otro lado se considera a Tsagantegia puede ser un Shamosaurinae o un Ankylosaurinae básico.

facts.statement: No additional remains of Tsagantegia longicranialis have been found or mentioned in scientific literature since its description.
facts.quote: Since its description, no additional remains of Tsagantegia longicranialis have been mentioned in scientific literature.

facts.statement: Palatal comparisons show Tsagantegia had a shovel-shaped mouth, unlike the wide rectangular snout of the contemporary Talarurus.
facts.quote: En una vista palatal, el rostro Talarurus tiene una forma rectangular ancha, mientras que Tsagantegia tienen una boca más en forma de pala.

facts.statement: Morphological differences indicate Tsagantegia filled the niche of a browsing herbivore, while Talarurus was a grazer.
facts.quote: Estas diferencias morfológicas indican que Tsagantegia llenaba el nicho de un herbívoro ramoneador, mientras que Talarurus era un pastador.

facts.statement: Caliche layers indicate a semi-arid climate, while fluvial and lacustrine sediments suggest the presence of large rivers and lakes.
facts.quote: El límite a base de caliche indica un ambiente y clima semiárido, pero también, la presencia de sedimentos fluviales y lacustres son indicadores de grandes ríos y lagos.

facts.statement: Fossil fruit remains found at Bor Guvé and Khara Khutul suggest the presence of angiosperm plants in the area.
facts.quote: Además de esto, se han recuperado restos de frutas fósiles de las localidades de Bor Guvé y Khara Khutul, Alto y Bajo Bayan Shireh, respectivamente, lo que sugiere la presencia de plantas angiospermas.

facts.statement: Tsagantegia shared its habitat with various dinosaurs and non-dinosaurs including theropods like Achillobator and Alectrosaurus, the ankylosaurid Talarurus, marginocephalians like Amtocephale and Graciliceratops, the hadrosauroid Gobihadros, and the sauropod Erketu.
facts.quote: Tsagantegia compartió su hábitat con numerosos animales de otras localidades de la formación, comprometiendo géneros de dinosaurios y no dinosaurios como los terópodos Achillobator, Alectrosaurus, Erlikosaurus, Garudimimus y Segnosaurus, el relativo anquilosáurido Talarurus, marginocéfalos como Amtocephale y Graciliceratops, el hadrosauroide Gobihadros, y el gran saurópodo Erketu.

facts.statement: Tsagantegia belongs to the parent group Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ankylosaurinae

facts.statement: Tsagantegia is a member of the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Tsagantegia is Tsagantegia longicranialis.
facts.quote: Type species: Tsagantegia longicranialis

facts.statement: Tsagantegia lived from the Cenomanian to the Santonian, approximately 100.5 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Santonian (100.5 to 83.6 million years ago)
